program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding deep passes; consolidate and run heavy validation after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Direct PubMed/NCBI discovery and sequential abstract verification
PMID-level dedupe against cumulative Wave 2100 deep selection

waves.title: The therapeutic potential of N-acetylcysteine across multiple organ systems: a narrative review.
waves.study: narrative review of preclinical and clinical literature
waves.population: mixed respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, neurologic, and perioperative populations
waves.finding: NAC has broad antioxidant and anti-inflammatory plausibility and condition-specific clinical signals, but trial results across organ systems are mixed and inconsistent.
waves.safety: Narrative synthesis and variable doses, formulations, and populations do not support a single broad therapeutic claim; gastrointestinal adverse effects were the most commonly noted.

waves.title: Safety and efficacy of liposomal iron for iron deficiency anemia in pediatric population: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.finding: Liposomal iron was generally non-inferior to conventional oral iron, showed a larger hemoglobin increase at six months, and caused fewer adverse events and less constipation.
waves.safety: Evidence remains preliminary with substantial heterogeneity for some endpoints and only four trials; formulation-specific benefit should not be generalized to all iron products.

waves.title: Administration of N-acetylcysteine influence the expression of apoptotic genes in the granulosa cells of infertile women diagnosed with endometriosis.
waves.finding: NAC increased serum antioxidant markers and shifted granulosa-cell apoptosis-related gene expression toward reduced apoptosis versus placebo.
waves.safety: This tiny mechanistic study did not establish fertility, pregnancy, or live-birth benefit; gene-expression changes should not be promoted as clinical efficacy.

waves.title: Vitamin D Status and Supplementation in Chronic Rhinosinusitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis; 15 status studies plus 4 RCTs of supplementation
waves.finding: CRS patients had lower vitamin-D levels than controls; supplementation improved SNOT-22 symptoms before three months but the benefit was not maintained at longer follow-up.
waves.safety: Low vitamin-D status association and short-term treatment signal should be kept distinct; durable efficacy remains unproven.

waves.title: Maternal Iodine Status During Pregnancy and Child Neurodevelopment: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis of Prospective Cohort Studies.
waves.study: systematic review/dose-response meta-analysis of 8 independent prospective cohorts
waves.finding: Suboptimal maternal iodine status was associated with modestly poorer child neurodevelopment, particularly cognition; exploratory fitted curves were most favorable in a mid-range of iodine intake.
waves.safety: This is observational exposure evidence, not proof that supplementation improves neurodevelopment; nonlinearity was not statistically robust after cohort consolidation.

waves.title: Vitamins and nutraceuticals in glaucoma research.
waves.study: comprehensive narrative review of 35 vitamins, minerals, and nutraceuticals
waves.population: glaucoma research spanning experimental and clinical evidence
waves.finding: Multiple nutrients and nutraceuticals have plausible retinal-neuroprotection or pressure-related mechanisms, but the strength and clinical maturity of evidence varies greatly by compound.
waves.safety: This review is useful for evidence mapping, not as proof that nutraceuticals prevent or treat glaucoma.

waves.title: Efficacy and safety of microneedling with tranexamic acid versus microneedling with vitamin C in the treatment of melasma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Microneedling with vitamin C and with tranexamic acid produced comparable short-term pigment outcomes; the pooled difference was not statistically significant.
waves.safety: Procedural transdermal vitamin-C evidence is not evidence for oral supplementation; follow-up was short and equivalence was not formally established.

waves.title: Effect of sesame oil and Nigella sativa oil on the prevention of amiodarone-induced phlebitis: a randomized controlled trial.
waves.finding: Topical Nigella sativa oil and sesame oil reduced incidence and severity of infusion-related phlebitis versus no topical intervention, with sesame showing the lowest rate.
waves.safety: This is topical catheter-site care, not evidence for oral black-seed supplementation or systemic cardiovascular benefit.

waves.title: Dietary Polyphenols and Selected Nutraceuticals in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Mechanistic Insights, Translational Evidence, and Clinical Prospects.
waves.population: HCC evidence spanning epidemiology, experimental models, and limited clinical studies
waves.finding: Polyphenols and selected nutraceuticals affect multiple carcinogenesis pathways in preclinical systems, but clinical translation is constrained by poor bioavailability, formulation variability, and lack of high-quality trials.
waves.safety: Mechanistic anticancer plausibility must not be presented as clinical treatment efficacy or as a substitute for oncology therapy.

waves.title: Impact of Melatonin Supplementation on Glycemic Parameters in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Melatonin supplementation reduced fasting glucose, insulin, HbA1c, and HOMA-IR in pooled analyses.
waves.safety: Small evidence base and exploratory duration/dose subgroup results do not establish an optimal regimen; larger trials are needed.

waves.title: Probiotic mediated modulation of neonatal health: a meta-analysis of prematurity-related morbidity, jaundice, and respiratory distress.
waves.finding: Probiotic supplementation was associated with less neonatal jaundice, lower peak bilirubin, less phototherapy, lower respiratory-distress incidence, and shorter respiratory support.
waves.safety: Moderate heterogeneity, strain/dose variability, and limited long-term safety data preclude standardized routine-use recommendations.

waves.title: Meta-analysis of the efficacy and safety of L-carnitine and N-acetylcysteine monotherapy for male idiopathic infertility.
waves.finding: L-carnitine and NAC monotherapy improved several semen parameters in pooled analyses; L-carnitine also increased testosterone, while other hormones were unchanged.
waves.safety: Semen surrogate improvements do not establish pregnancy or live-birth benefit, and the two antioxidants should not be treated as interchangeable.

waves.title: Role of the EPA: DHA dosing ratio in omega-3 supplements on blood fatty acid profiles and inflammation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: healthy and clinical populations receiving EPA+DHA supplements
waves.finding: EPA:DHA ratio influenced blood fatty-acid composition and pooled inflammatory markers, with different ratios favoring different biochemical outcomes.
waves.safety: Ratio/dose subgroup findings are formulation-level meta-analytic associations, not validated personalized dosing rules.

waves.title: Ginkgo diterpene lactone meglumine for functional recovery in patients with acute ischemic stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.population: patients with acute ischemic stroke receiving conventional treatment
waves.finding: Ginkgo diterpene lactone meglumine added to conventional treatment improved 90-day functional-outcome measures in pooled trials.
waves.safety: This is an injectable Chinese patent medicine/formulation used adjunctively in acute stroke, not evidence for oral generic Ginkgo biloba supplements.

waves.title: The effect of caffeine consumption on age-related macular degeneration: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review of 5 observational studies; 9,318 patients
waves.population: adults evaluated for AMD development or progression
waves.finding: Caffeine intake was not significantly associated with early or late AMD development; limited vote-counting suggested a possible progression benefit, largely from tea consumption.
waves.safety: Observational beverage evidence is sparse and confounded; tea-associated signals should not be attributed to caffeine itself.

waves.title: Effects of probiotic supplementation on glycemic control in children with type 1 diabetes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Probiotics reduced HbA1c and insulin requirements in pooled analyses, while fasting glucose reduction was not significant; formulation subgrouping explained much between-study variance.
waves.safety: Small pediatric evidence base and strong formulation dependence require cautious adjunctive interpretation.

waves.title: Effect of multistrain probiotics on symptom severity in irritable bowel syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of irritable bowel syndrome-symptom severity score outcomes.
waves.finding: Multistrain probiotics reduced total IBS symptom-severity scores and several subscores, but did not consistently improve abdominal pain or IBS-specific quality of life.
waves.safety: Heterogeneity was extreme for most outcomes, so pooled averages should not be generalized across multistrain products.

waves.title: Meta-analysis of probiotic metabolites in the prevention of gestational weight gain and postpartum weight retention.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of 46 RCTs; over 12,500 pregnant women
waves.finding: Probiotic supplementation was associated with lower gestational weight gain and postpartum weight retention and modest improvements in several metabolic markers.
waves.safety: Substantial strain, dose, and duration heterogeneity means the pooled effect cannot define a standardized prenatal probiotic regimen.

waves.title: The therapeutic readiness of probiotics in major depressive disorder: A systematic review of randomised controlled trials.
waves.study: systematic review of 13 double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs; 437 adults
waves.population: adults with clinically diagnosed major depressive disorder
waves.finding: Most trials reported modest adjunctive symptom benefit, most consistently in younger outpatients with mild-to-moderate MDD and multi-strain Lactobacillus/Bifidobacterium formulations.
waves.safety: Context, geography, strain composition, and trial design strongly affected findings; evidence supports at most individualized adjunctive use, not class-wide antidepressant efficacy.

waves.title: Effectiveness and safety of turmeric for the treatment of COVID-19: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: patients with mild-to-severe COVID-19, mostly hospitalized
waves.finding: Turmeric interventions, commonly nano-curcumin adjuncts, were associated with lower mortality, less mechanical ventilation, less deterioration, and greater symptom resolution in pooled trials.
waves.safety: Formulation-specific adjunctive evidence with multiple high-risk-of-bias trials should not be generalized to ordinary turmeric supplements or substitute for antiviral/medical care.

waves.title: The Effect of Diet and Dietary Supplements on Iron Status of Active Females: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Interventional Trials.
waves.population: physically active females of reproductive age
waves.finding: Ferrous-sulfate supplementation significantly increased hemoglobin and ferritin in active females.
waves.safety: Findings apply to iron-status interventions in a population at elevated deficiency risk and do not support indiscriminate iron use in iron-replete athletes.

waves.title: Effect of iron therapy on fatigue symptoms in non-anaemic iron deficient women of reproductive age- A Randomized Controlled Trial.
waves.population: non-anemic iron-deficient women age 18–45 with fatigue
waves.finding: Two months of iron therapy reduced fatigue and increased ferritin and hemoglobin relative to baseline/placebo comparisons reported by the trial.
waves.safety: Benefit is specific to documented iron deficiency despite absence of anemia; iron treatment should not be generalized to fatigue without deficiency.

waves.title: Effect of Calcium Citrate Versus Calcium Carbonate on Parathyroid Hormone Levels in Patients Undergoing Bariatric Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
waves.finding: Calcium citrate produced better single-dose calcium exposure and PTH suppression than calcium carbonate, but chronic interventions showed no significant PTH difference between formulations.
waves.safety: Acute pharmacokinetic superiority should not be presented as proven long-term clinical superiority.

waves.title: The impact of maternal vitamin D levels during pregnancy and risk of autism spectrum disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder diagnosis and symptoms in offspring: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/dose-response meta-analysis of 15 observational studies
waves.population: pregnant women and offspring assessed for ASD/ADHD outcomes
waves.finding: Higher maternal vitamin-D status was associated with modestly lower ASD and ADHD risk/symptom estimates in observational analyses.
waves.safety: Maternal vitamin-D status is an exposure biomarker; association does not establish that supplementation prevents ASD or ADHD.

waves.title: [Nutraceuticals in the clinical management of women with breast cancer; a narrative review].
waves.population: women with or surviving breast cancer
waves.finding: The review surveys nutraceutical use for symptom and quality-of-life management around breast-cancer treatment, reflecting widespread use but heterogeneous clinical evidence.
waves.safety: Cancer-treatment interactions and variable evidence quality require compound-specific clinical review; a broad nutraceutical category cannot be assumed safe or effective.
